title: 11 Whisperwake Isles Aniimo You Should Know | Skills, Builds and Teams | Aniimo Guide
description: Eleven Aniimo from the Whisperwake Isles explained: Reefish, Coraliz, Bubbeep, Glameep, Malangel, Malevsera, Fennelun, Cozite, Gachapus, Dewple, Mesmerowl and Pouchwisp. Skills, roles and team tips, checked against aniimo.gg and Aniimo Wiki in November 2026.

sections.heading: Intro
sections.script: Whisperwake Isles is packed with Aniimo that most players have not looked at closely yet. In this video we go through eleven of them, from the coral dwelling Reefish line to the coin tossing Pouchwisp. For each one you will hear what element it is, where it lives, which skills make it special and how it fits into a team. Everything comes from the in game skill text and two fan reference sites, checked in November. Some Aniimo are healers, some are damage dealers and some boost the whole team, so there is something for every squad. Take notes as we go, because several of these Aniimo combine well with each other, and a few have Alpha boss forms that make great hunting targets once your team is ready. Stay until the end, because the last section helps you pick where to start.

sections.heading: Reefish and Coraliz
sections.script: Let's begin with the Rock and Water family. Reefish is a stage one Aniimo that you can find around Crescent Bay in the Whisperwake Isles. It burrows underground so it looks like a patch of coral, then bites whatever wanders close. It can swim, and its coral trap hits for power sixty seven and costs twenty energy while stacking an Earth debuff. Reefish evolves into Coraliz, a stage three Rock and Water Aniimo with an Alpha boss form. Coraliz applies a Coral Mark for six seconds, and when the mark ends the target takes extra damage equal to three Might for every hit of Earth damage it took. Bring other Earth attackers to make that bonus count.

sections.heading: Bubbeep and Glameep
sections.script: Next up are the healers. Bubbeep is a Grass and Water support Aniimo that lives around Crescent Bay. It chews algae and turns it into floating bubbles, then rides those bubbles around, and yes, it can swim. Baa Bubble Wave launches a bubble that shields allies along its path, while Ripples of Floating Duckweed heals your team inside a moving area. Bubbeep evolves into Glameep, a stage three healer with the same kit and a stronger body. Glameep also has a Prismana form, and there is an Omega Glameep boss version to challenge. If your team keeps running out of health, this line is a strong answer, especially on long fights where steady healing and shields matter more than raw damage.

sections.heading: Malangel and Malevsera
sections.script: Now a pair of Ice Aniimo with a mean streak. Malangel greets targets with a cheerful smile and sneaks up on them, then once the fight starts it bares its fangs. It evolves into Malevsera, a stage three Ice Aniimo that looks gentler than it fights. Both of them do Artisanship in the Homeland, at level one for Malangel and level three for Malevsera, so the evolution is a real upgrade for crafting too. The fan site Aniimo gg lists Glacy as a good partner, and the Aniimo Wiki files this line as an Ice damage dealer. It is a nice pick if you like fast, aggressive Ice teams, and a good way to put your crafting skills to use while you fight.

sections.heading: Fennelun
sections.script: Fennelun is a stage three Light Aniimo with soft moonlight running through its fur, and it even has an Alpha boss form. Its kit is all about the Fox Mark. Lumin Bolts fires three Light missiles at different targets and applies Fox Mark, which lowers their Light resistance. Moon Impact drops a full moon on the target for power forty five at fifteen energy, and it deals extra area damage when it hits a marked enemy. Lunar Eclipse pours moonlight onto the target for heavy extra Break damage. Mark first, drop the moon second, finish with the eclipse, and you have a clean combo.

sections.heading: Cozite
sections.script: Cozite is a humble stage one Rock Aniimo, but it has a lot of charm. It builds its shell bit by bit out of mud, and when danger shows up it sprays smoke from the hole on top to hide itself. In combat it kicks a Rolling Mud Ball for power thirty one that deals area damage on impact, and you can hold the button to aim and lob it. Shielding Smoke costs only ten energy and enemies cannot aim through the cloud. Cozite can fly and glide, does Hauling at level one in the Homeland, and evolves into Bailite later on.

sections.heading: Gachapus
sections.script: Gachapus belongs to the Popapus line and it is a stage three Water Aniimo that you can meet in the Whisperwake Isles. It works like a capsule machine. With a quick tap of its tentacles it launches colourful capsule bubbles from its head, and every attack adds another colour to its gacha slots. Bubble Barrage keeps spitting bubbles at the target for five seconds. Rigged Draw uses up the bubbles of your least common colour, then the next basic attack fires the most common colour with a wider area and extra damage. It rewards you for planning, and it is a lot of fun to play.

sections.heading: Dewple
sections.script: Dewple is a stage three Water Aniimo made of several small Dewlops that drift apart now and then, yet always move together and follow the biggest one. It supports the team instead of just attacking. Tide Resonance gives your whole squad a Water damage boost. Whirlpool Dewdrop creates a whirlpool that pulls enemies toward the centre once. Current Jet blasts a straight line, and each hit can spend two stacks of Water Debuff to add damage equal to fifty percent of Might. There is also an Alpha Dewple out there to hunt. It is a great fit for a Water team, because the boost helps every attacker standing beside it, not only Dewple itself.

sections.heading: Mesmerowl
sections.script: Mesmerowl is a stage three Wind Aniimo that beats its ear feather wings while it patrols low over its territory. It can fly and glide. Mesmerwave Recharge releases a bewildering wave that raises your team's energy recovery rate, and the effect gets stronger against targets that are bewildered or in a Break state. Wind Blade Strikes fires four extra blades after charging, and each hit lowers the target's energy recovery. Wind Bomb Therapy bounces a bomb off the target and back to Mesmerowl, healing the whole team when it returns. An Alpha Mesmerowl exists as well.

sections.heading: Pouchwisp
sections.script: Pouchwisp looks like a giant springy coin pouch full of tiny Pennywisps, and it is a stage three Dark Aniimo. It seems to toss gold around, but it is really letting the Pennywisps out to play. Coin Boost places a Pennywisp Mark on a target, and if that target is broken or defeated the mark jumps to another enemy nearby and restores energy to Pouchwisp. Showhand throws a giant Coinwisp that explodes in an area, and the lower the target's health, the more damage it deals. High Roller Toss can charm nearby targets. There is an Alpha Pouchwisp too.

sections.heading: Which one first
sections.script: So which one should you start with? If you want to heal and shield, go for Bubbeep and grow it into Glameep. For team buffs, Dewple and Mesmerowl are the picks. If you love combos, try Fennelun or Coraliz. And if you want something stylish, Pouchwisp and Gachapus are packed with personality. Remember that every Aniimo here lives in or near the Whisperwake Isles, so one trip can fill your team. Which of these eleven is your favourite, and which one are you catching first? Tell us in the comments, and subscribe to HarryBeast Gaming for more Aniimo guides every day.
